8	/-!
9	# Chart finiteness is not a restriction — it is UNSATISFIABLE on a curve
10	
11	`ChiUnconditional.lean` refutes the one-point bump `hbump` and the closed χ-ledger `hledger`
12	on any two-set cover having a prime divisor off one chart.  Both refutations carry the binder
13	
14	`[∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]`
15	
16	at a **non-total** open `U₀`, and that file's `ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` describes it
17	as "a substantive geometric restriction" which "has already excluded the curves
18	Riemann–Roch is about".  `WeilDivisor.lean:1271-1280` reads the same binder as ruling out
19	"a class of covers, not the ledger", and concludes the open work is to *exhibit a cover on
20	which the ledger can hold*.
21	
22	**This file shows there is no such cover, and the reason is one step of commutative algebra
23	rather than anything about covers.**  A single instance of the binder — at the zero divisor
24	alone, not the whole family — already forces `K(X)` to be a finite extension of `k`:
25	
26	`Adelic.module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite`:
27	  `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U 0) → Module.Finite k K(X)`, for a nonempty affine `U`.
28	
29	The mechanism: `sectionSub k U 0` is exactly the set of rational functions with
30	`ord_P ≥ 0` at every prime divisor meeting `U`.  That set is a **subring** (orders add under
31	multiplication, `sectionSub_mul_mem_zero`) and it **contains the chart ring** `Γ(X, U)`
32	(chart-integral elements have nonnegative order, `order_algebraMap_chart_nonneg`).  A
33	`k`-finite domain is a field (`fieldOfFiniteDimensional`), and a subfield of `K(X)`
34	containing `Γ(X, U)` — whose fraction field is `K(X)` (`chartRing_isFractionRing`) — is all
35	of `K(X)`.
36	
37	## Why this sharpens the refutations rather than weakening them
38	
39	The refutations of `hbump`/`hledger` remain true and remain proved.  What changes is their
40	**reading**.  They were presented as "the ledger is false on covers of this kind, so look for
41	a better cover".  The honest reading is stronger and simpler:
42	
43	* On a curve with a nonconstant function, `K(X)/k` is *not* finite (a nonconstant function is
44	  transcendental over the constants), so the chart-finiteness binder is **satisfied at no
45	  such curve, on any cover, with any charts**.  Hence the §5–§6 refutations of
46	  `ChiUnconditional.lean` are — on a curve — refutations with unsatisfiable hypotheses.
47	* So the bump route is not "dead on bad covers"; the *refutation* of it is vacuous on curves.
48	  Neither `hbump` nor `hledger` has been shown false at a curve. They are **open**, not
49	  refuted, and the search for "a cover on which the ledger can hold" is not the open problem.
50	
51	This is trap (c) of `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` applied to a *negative* result, which is the
52	case the trap catalogue did not cover: a refutation whose own hypotheses are unsatisfiable
53	tells you nothing about the statement it refutes.  Both the refutation and its retraction
54	report clean axioms.
55	
56	`chart_finiteness_iff_module_finite_functionField` states the equivalence, so the binder is
57	visibly interchangeable with a hypothesis about `k ⊆ K(X)` alone — no cover, no charts, no
58	divisors.
59	
60	## The `⊤` binders used everywhere else in the lane are NOT affected — and here is why
61	
62	This matters more than the negative result itself, because if the argument reached `⊤` it would
63	demolish `GlobalGeneration.lean`, `LedgerClosure.lean` and `SectionBounds.lean` as well, all of
64	which assume `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)`.  The dividing line is visible in the
65	signature: **`IsAffineOpen U` is load-bearing**, used exactly once, for
66	`chartRing_isFractionRing` — the step that identifies `K(X)` as the fraction field of the chart
67	ring.
68	
69	**The precise statement, and it is NOT "⊤ is safe".**  What decides the matter is whether `⊤` is
70	affine, i.e. whether `X` is affine — *not* whether `U` is written `⊤`:
71	
72	* On a **proper** curve `⊤` is not affine, `chartRing_isFractionRing` is unavailable there, and
73	  the collapse does not run.  This is the case the `hledger`-consuming results are *about*, and
74	  their `⊤` binders survive.
75	* On an **affine** `X` with a prime divisor, `isAffineOpen_top` applies and
76	  `not_chart_finite_of_primeDivisor` kills the `⊤` binder as well.  Machine-checked, not
77	  reasoned: `not_chart_finite_of_primeDivisor k (isAffineOpen_top X) P` elaborates.
78	
79	That second bullet is a real caveat rather than a curiosity, because the consumers in
80	`GlobalGeneration.lean`, `LedgerClosure.lean` and `SectionBounds.lean` are stated for a **bare
81	`Scheme X`** with no `IsProper` binder anywhere.  So their `⊤` binders are unsatisfiable on the
82	affine members of the family they quantify over.  They are not thereby wrong or useless — at a
83	proper curve, the case of interest, the binder is exactly the finiteness of `L(D)` that
84	Riemann–Roch asserts — but a consumer instantiating them at an affine scheme gets a vacuous
85	statement, and no docstring in that lane says so.
86	
87	The honest asymmetry, stated with the hypothesis it needs: at a **proper** curve,
88	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)` is finiteness of `L(D)`, which Riemann–Roch asserts, while
89	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)` at an affine chart is a disguised finiteness of `K(X)/k`,
90	which is false.  Drop properness and the distinction collapses with it.
91	
92	`ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` is the one to compare: it needs no cover and no affineness, so
93	it applies at any `U`, but its *conclusion* is vacuous when `U = ⊤` (`ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(E)` with the tower
94	frozen is then no restriction at all). The bite comes only from a non-total open, which is
95	precisely where affineness is available and the binder collapses.
96	
97	## What this file does NOT claim
98	
99	It does not prove `hbump` or `hledger` — those are now *open* at a curve rather than refuted,
100	which is a statement about the state of knowledge, not a proof of either.
101	
102	**The residual input IS discharged, and more cheaply than first expected.**  An earlier
103	version of this header said proving `K(X)/k` infinite "needs a nonconstant rational function,
104	which is `NonconstantToP1.lean` territory and is not wired in here".  That turned out to be
105	unnecessary: `not_module_finite_functionField_of_primeDivisor` gets it from the existence of a
106	**single prime divisor**, with no polynomial argument and no morphism to `ℙ¹`.  The DVR stalk
107	`𝒪_P` sits between `k` and `K(X)`; finiteness would make it a `k`-finite domain, hence a field,
108	and `exists_order_eq` produces an element of order `1` whose inverse has order `-1` and so
109	cannot lie in it.  A discrete valuation ring is not a field.
110	
111	So `not_chart_finite_of_primeDivisor` is the unconditional statement: on a curve with a prime
112	divisor and a nonempty affine chart, the binder holds nowhere.  The
113	`_of_transcendental` variants are kept as the general field-theoretic form.
114	
115	## The three cluster-P gaps, kept apart
116	
117	Unchanged by this file, and this file touches only the first:

119	* **Single-field vanishing** — open. This file removes a *false lead* (repairing the cover)

122	  proved at no curve, strictly stronger than the single-field count.
123	* **Global generation** — untouched. Still ledger-conditional in `GlobalGeneration.lean`.

179	theorem algebraMap_chart_mem_sectionSub_zero {U : X.Opens} [Nonempty U] (r : Γ(X, U)) :
180	    algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField r ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) := by
181	  rcases eq_or_ne (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField r) 0 with h0 | h0
182	  · rw [h0]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
183	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
184	  change -((0 : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ) P) ≤ _
185	  simp only [Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply, neg_zero]
186	  exact order_algebraMap_chart_nonneg P hP r

188	/-- **`Γ(U, 𝒪(0))` is closed under multiplication.**  Orders add
189	(`order_mul_of_ne_zero`), so two functions with nonnegative order at each prime meeting `U`
190	have a product with the same property.  This is what makes the section space at the *zero*
191	divisor a ring, and it is the step that turns a finiteness binder into a field. -/
192	theorem sectionSub_mul_mem_zero (U : X.Opens) {f g : X.functionField}
193	    (hf : f ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor))
194	    (hg : g ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) :
195	    f * g ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) := by
196	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
197	  · simp only [zero_mul]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
198	  rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hg0
199	  · simp only [mul_zero]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
200	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
201	  rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P hf0 hg0]
202	  have h1 := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf P hP
203	  have h2 := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hg0).mp hg P hP
204	  change -((0 : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ) P) ≤ _ at h1 h2
205	  change -((0 : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ) P) ≤ _
206	  simp only [Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply, neg_zero] at h1 h2 ⊢
207	  linarith

210	`sectionSub_mul_mem_zero` plus `1 ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪(0))` upgrade the `k`-submodule to a subalgebra.
211	Its being a *ring* is what converts a finiteness binder into a field, which is the whole
212	mechanism of this file. -/
213	def chartAlg (U : X.Opens) : Subalgebra k X.functionField where
214	  carrier := sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)
215	  mul_mem' := sectionSub_mul_mem_zero k U
216	  one_mem' := one_mem_sectionOfDivisor_zero U
217	  add_mem' := (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)).add_mem
218	  zero_mem' := (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)).zero_mem
219	  algebraMap_mem' := fun c => by
220	    have h1 : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) :=
221	      one_mem_sectionOfDivisor_zero U
222	    have := (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)).smul_mem c h1

226	    f ∈ chartAlg k U ↔ f ∈ sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) := Iff.rfl

229	chart, `K(X) = Frac Γ(X, U)` (`chartRing_isFractionRing`), so every `f : K(X)` is `a/b` with
230	`a, b ∈ Γ(X, U) ⊆ chartAlg`.  Inside a field, `b⁻¹` is available, so `f = a·b⁻¹` lies in
231	`chartAlg` too. -/
232	theorem chartAlg_eq_top_of_isField {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U]
233	    (hfield : IsField (chartAlg k U)) : chartAlg k U = ⊤ := by
234	  haveI hfr : IsFractionRing Γ(X, U) X.functionField := chartRing_isFractionRing hU
235	  refine Algebra.eq_top_iff.mpr fun f => ?_
236	  obtain ⟨a, b, hb, hab⟩ := IsFractionRing.div_surjective (A := Γ(X, U)) f

238	    algebraMap_chart_mem_sectionSub_zero k a

240	    algebraMap_chart_mem_sectionSub_zero k b
241	  have hbne : algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField b ≠ 0 := fun h =>
242	    (nonZeroDivisors.coe_ne_zero ⟨b, hb⟩) (IsFractionRing.to_map_eq_zero_iff.mp h)
243	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hfield.mul_inv_cancel (a := (⟨_, hb'⟩ : chartAlg k U))

245	  have hbinv : (algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField b)⁻¹ ∈ chartAlg k U := by
246	    have hval : algebraMap Γ(X, U) X.functionField b * (c : X.functionField) = 1 := by
247	      have := congrArg (fun z : chartAlg k U => (z : X.functionField)) hc
248	      simpa using this
249	    rw [← eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_right hval]; exact c.2
250	  rw [← hab, div_eq_mul_inv]
251	  exact Subalgebra.mul_mem _ ha' hbinv

253	/-- **THE MAIN RESULT — chart finiteness at the ZERO divisor already forces `K(X)/k` finite.**
254	
255	One instance of the binder that `ChiUnconditional.lean`'s refutations quantify over the whole
256	divisor family — `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U 0)` at a single nonempty affine chart — is
257	enough to collapse the function field onto a finite extension of `k`.
258	
259	Chain: `Γ(U, 𝒪(0))` is a `k`-finite domain (`chartAlg`), hence a field
260	(`fieldOfFiniteDimensional`); a field between `Γ(X, U)` and its own fraction field is
261	everything (`chartAlg_eq_top_of_isField`); so `K(X)` *is* that finite `k`-module.
262	
263	**Why this is the sharp statement.** `ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` says chart finiteness
264	bounds `ℓ` along a tower and calls that "a substantive geometric restriction". It is not a
265	restriction on the *cover* at all — no cover appears in this statement. It is a restriction on
266	`k ⊆ K(X)`, which no choice of charts can change. -/
267	theorem module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
268	    [Nonempty U] (hfin : Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor))) :
269	    Module.Finite k X.functionField := by
270	  haveI hfd : FiniteDimensional k (chartAlg k U) := hfin
271	  have htop : chartAlg k U = ⊤ :=
272	    chartAlg_eq_top_of_isField k hU (fieldOfFiniteDimensional k (chartAlg k U)).toIsField
273	  exact Module.Finite.equiv
274	    ((Subalgebra.equivOfEq _ _ htop).toLinearEquiv.trans
275	      (Subalgebra.topEquiv (R := k) (A := X.functionField)).toLinearEquiv)
276	
277	/-- **The binder is EQUIVALENT to a statement with no cover, no chart and no divisor in it.**
278	Forward is `module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite`; backward, a `k`-submodule of a
279	`k`-finite space is `k`-finite.  Stating the equivalence is the point: it makes visible that
280	supplying the chart-finiteness binder is *exactly* assuming `K(X)/k` finite, and therefore that
281	no cleverness about covers or charts can ever satisfy it on a curve. -/
282	theorem chart_finiteness_iff_module_finite_functionField {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
283	    [Nonempty U] :
284	    Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) ↔ Module.Finite k X.functionField := by
285	  refine ⟨fun h => module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite k hU h, fun h => ?_⟩
286	  exact Module.Finite.of_injective (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)).subtype
287	    Subtype.val_injective
288	
289	omit [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] [IsConstantField k X] in
290	/-- **What closing this costs, as one hypothesis.**  If some `f : K(X)` is transcendental over
291	`k` then `K(X)/k` is not finite, so — by
292	`chart_finiteness_iff_module_finite_functionField` — the chart-finiteness binder fails at
293	*every* nonempty affine chart, and with it every §5–§6 refutation of `ChiUnconditional.lean`.
294	
295	The hypothesis is exactly "the curve has a nonconstant function". AJC constructs such a
296	function in `NonconstantToP1.lean` for its own curve; wiring that in is downstream of this
297	module and is deliberately left as this named input rather than assumed here.
298	
299	Pure field theory — no geometry is used, hence the `omit`. -/
300	theorem not_module_finite_functionField_of_transcendental
301	    (f : X.functionField) (hf : ¬ IsAlgebraic k f) :
302	    ¬ Module.Finite k X.functionField := fun hfin => by
303	  haveI : FiniteDimensional k X.functionField := hfin
304	  exact hf (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral f).isAlgebraic

306	/-- **The order-nonnegative subring at a prime divisor `P`, as a `k`-subalgebra of `K(X)`.**

309	what makes the residual input of this file discharge with no transcendence hypothesis. -/
310	def valSubalg (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : Subalgebra k X.functionField where
311	  carrier := orderGeSub k P 0
312	  mul_mem' := by
313	    intro f g hf hg
314	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
315	    · simp only [zero_mul]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
316	    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hg0
317	    · simp only [mul_zero]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
318	    refine Or.inr ?_
319	    rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P hf0 hg0]
320	    have h1 := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf
321	    have h2 := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hg0).mp hg
322	    linarith
323	  one_mem' := Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one])
324	  add_mem' := (orderGeSub k P 0).add_mem
325	  zero_mem' := (orderGeSub k P 0).zero_mem
326	  algebraMap_mem' := fun c => by
327	    have h1 : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P 0 :=
328	      Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one])
329	    have := (orderGeSub k P 0).smul_mem c h1
330	    rwa [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one] at this
331	
332	/-- **`K(X)/k` IS NOT FINITE as soon as ONE prime divisor exists — no transcendence
333	hypothesis needed.**
334	
335	This discharges the residual input of this module outright.  The argument needs no polynomial
336	and no nonconstant morphism: if `K(X)/k` were finite then the order-nonnegative subring `𝒪_P`
337	(`valSubalg`) would be a `k`-finite domain, hence a **field** — but `exists_order_eq` supplies
338	`t` with `ord_P t = 1`, and `t · u = 1` forces `ord_P u = -1 < 0`, contradicting membership in
339	`𝒪_P`.  In one line: *a discrete valuation ring is not a field, and finiteness over `k` would
340	make it one.*

343	`Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne` is about, and it is far weaker than a nonconstant map to
344	`ℙ¹`: a curve without prime divisors has nothing for `sectionSub` to read. -/

348	  haveI : FiniteDimensional k X.functionField := hfin
349	  haveI : FiniteDimensional k (valSubalg k P) :=
350	    Module.Finite.of_injective (valSubalg k P).toSubmodule.subtype Subtype.val_injective
351	  have hfield : IsField (valSubalg k P) := (fieldOfFiniteDimensional k (valSubalg k P)).toIsField
352	  obtain ⟨t, ht0, ht⟩ := exists_order_eq P 1
353	  have htmem : t ∈ valSubalg k P := Or.inr (by rw [ht]; norm_num)
354	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hfield.mul_inv_cancel (a := (⟨t, htmem⟩ : valSubalg k P))
355	    (by simp only [ne_eq, Subtype.ext_iff]; exact ht0)
356	  have hval : t * (u : X.functionField) = 1 := by
357	    have := congrArg (fun z : valSubalg k P => (z : X.functionField)) hu
358	    simpa using this
359	  have hu0 : (u : X.functionField) ≠ 0 := by
360	    intro h; rw [h, mul_zero] at hval; exact one_ne_zero hval.symm
361	  have hsum : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t
362	      + Scheme.RationalMap.order P (u : X.functionField) = 0 := by
363	    rw [← Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht0 hu0, hval,
364	      Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]
365	  have huge : 0 ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (u : X.functionField) :=
366	    (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hu0).mp u.2
367	  rw [ht] at hsum
368	  omega

370	/-- **THE UNCONDITIONAL FORM: the refutations' binder is satisfiable at NO curve with a prime
371	divisor.**  No transcendence hypothesis, no nonconstant map, no cover condition — a single
372	prime divisor plus a nonempty affine chart is enough.
373	
374	Combined with `ChiUnconditional.not_bump_of_notMem_left` and `ledger_refuted_of_notMem_left`
375	— whose hypotheses this contradicts — the conclusion is that those two theorems have **no
376	instances** on such a curve.  `hbump` and the closed χ-ledger are therefore **open** there,
377	not false, and the "find a better cover" reading of them is void. -/
378	theorem not_chart_finite_of_primeDivisor {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U]
379	    (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
380	    ¬ Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) := fun hfin =>

382	    (module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite k hU hfin)
383	
384	/-- **The refutations' binder is unsatisfiable on a curve with a nonconstant function.**  The

389	theorem not_chart_finite_of_transcendental {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U]
390	    (f : X.functionField) (hf : ¬ IsAlgebraic k f) :
391	    ¬ Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) := fun hfin =>
392	  not_module_finite_functionField_of_transcendental k f hf
393	    (module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite k hU hfin)

8	/-!
9	# The Čech Euler characteristic is an inclusion–exclusion count — unconditionally
10	
11	Every χ-statement in this lane so far has been *gated*: `ChiLedger.chi_add` and its
12	descendants take four exactness hypotheses (`window`, `connect`, `twist`, and the
13	surjectivity `htwist`) packaging the ledger four-term sequence
14	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0`, whose connecting map and
15	right-exactness the lane does not construct.  That is why `hbump` — "χ jumps by
16	`[κ(P):k]` at every one-point bump" — has been carried as an open hypothesis, and why
17	the audit at inbox `I-0449` was able to *refute* it off the cover overlap.
18	
19	This file removes the gate for the underlying numerical identity.  The point is that
20	for a **two-set cover** the Čech Euler characteristic needs no exact sequence at all:
21	
22	`χ(D) = dim 𝒞⁰(D) − dim 𝒞¹(D)` where `𝒞⁰(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊕ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))`,
23	`𝒞¹(D) = 𝒜(D) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, 𝒪(D))`,
24	
25	and both `ℓ(D) = dim ker` and `h¹(D) = dim coker` are read off the *same* map by
26	rank–nullity.  Concretely, with `B(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the coboundary and
27	`L(D) = Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁,𝒪(D))` the global sections (`Substrate.linearSystem_eq_inf`
28	on a cover), the modular law
29	`dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) = dim S₀ + dim S₁`
30	(mathlib's `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`) *is* the Euler characteristic:
31	
32	`χ(D) = ℓ(D) − h¹(D) = dim L(D) − (dim 𝒜(D) − dim B(D))`
33	      `= dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D) = dim S₀ + dim S₁ − dim 𝒜(D)`.
34	
35	## What is proved, and what it is worth
36	
37	* `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — **the unconditional χ formula.**
38	  `χ(D) = dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D)` on a cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
39	  with **no exactness hypotheses** — only the finiteness of the two chart section
40	  spaces.  This is strictly stronger than what `chi_add` gives, in the precise sense
41	  that it has none of `chi_add`'s four gated binders.
42	
43	* `chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` — the difference form: the χ-jump between two
44	  divisors is an alternating sum of three *local step* dimensions, again unconditionally.
45	
46	* `chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left` — at a point off one chart the whole χ-jump is the
47	  *single surviving chart step*, and `bump_iff_chartStep_of_notMem_left` makes the one-step
48	  bump equivalent to that step being full.  Both ungated.  These are one-step statements and
49	  must not be read as consistency claims — see the next item.
50	
51	* `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` and `not_bump_of_notMem_left` (§5) — `hbump` is FALSE
52	  **under this file's chart-finiteness binders** whenever some prime divisor's point lies off a
53	  chart.  Along the tower `n·P` both `Γ(U₀,−)` and `𝒜` freeze while `Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜` stays
54	  trapped, so χ is *bounded* — against `hbump`'s linear growth `n·[κ(P):k]`.  **READ THE NEXT
55	  SECTION BEFORE QUOTING THIS**: those binders are unsatisfiable on a curve, so this refutation
56	  does not reach a curve.  Earlier versions of this header called it "unconditional"; it is
57	  unconditional in *exactness data* only, never in the finiteness binders.
58	
59	* `ledger_refuted_of_notMem_left` (§6) — the same tower refutes the **closed ledger** `hledger`
60	  on such a cover, under the same binders and with the same caveat.
61	
62	## The finiteness binders are NOT innocent — and they are UNSATISFIABLE on a curve
63	
64	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)` at a **non-total** open `U` is a substantive restriction,
65	not bookkeeping.  The `ℓ`-level form is `ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower`:
66	
67	`ℓ(n·P + E) ≤ dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(E))` for all `n`, whenever `P.point ∉ U₀`
68	
69	— **it forbids Riemann growth outright**.
70	
71	**This was originally read as a restriction on the COVER, and that reading is wrong.**
72	`Adelic/ChartFinitenessRefuted.lean` proves that a *single* instance of the binder, at the zero
73	divisor alone, forces `K(X)` to be a **finite extension of `k`**
74	(`module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite`), and that the binder is *equivalent* to that
75	statement — one with no cover, no chart and no divisor in it
76	(`chart_finiteness_iff_module_finite_functionField`).  Mechanism: `Γ(U,𝒪(0))` is a ring
77	containing `Γ(X,U)`; a `k`-finite domain is a field; a field between `Γ(X,U)` and its own
78	fraction field is all of `K(X)`.
79	
80	Consequences, and they are the ones to carry forward:
81	
82	* On a curve with a nonconstant function the binder holds at **no chart and no cover**.  So
83	  §5–§6 refute nothing *about a curve*: `hbump` and `hledger` are **open** there, not false.
84	* "Exhibit a cover on which the ledger can hold" — the direction this file's earlier header and
85	  `WeilDivisor.lean` recommended — is **not** the open problem.  There is no cover to find.
86	* Prefer stating results at `⊤`, where `Module.Finite` is the honest finiteness of `L(D)`.
87	
88	This is trap (c) of `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` applied to a *negative* result, a case the
89	catalogue did not cover: a refutation whose own hypotheses are unsatisfiable reports clean
90	axioms exactly like a useful one.
91	
92	## Provenance
93	
94	Rederived in AJC's own abstractions (`sectionSub`, `chi`, `H1Mod`).  This is **not** a
95	port: the sibling project's `RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` core is a bounded
96	vanishing statement, not this identity, and nothing of this shape existed in either
97	project — the lane had only the gated `chi_add`.  The mathlib input is exactly one
98	lemma, `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`.
99	
100	## Correction history
101	
102	This module shipped, within one session, with docstrings claiming that the audit at inbox
103	`I-0449` had misfired and that `hbump` was *not* refutable off the overlap.  An adversarial
104	review (`I-0467`) showed the opposite from this file's own formula, and §5/§6 now carry the
105	refutations in Lean.  The retracted claim is left described rather than silently deleted, since
106	it was broadcast to two other teams before being corrected.
107	
108	**Third correction (task `ajc-rr`, 2026-07-28), and it goes the other way from the second.**
109	The refutations of §5–§6 were then presented as "unconditional" and as redirecting the route
110	towards a better cover.  Both readings were wrong, and the second one sent the next session at a
111	non-problem.  They are unconditional in *exactness data* only; their chart-finiteness binders are
112	unsatisfiable on a curve (`ChartFinitenessRefuted.lean`), so on a curve the refutations are
113	vacuous and `hbump`/`hledger` are open rather than false.  The theorems are unchanged and still
114	true — only their scope was overstated.  Pattern worth naming, since this module has now
115	produced it twice in opposite directions: "not refutable by this route" does not give "fine",
116	and "refuted under my binders" does not give "refuted".
117	-/

137	theorem sectionSub_top_eq_inf (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
138	    sectionSub k ⊤ D = sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D := by
139	  apply SetLike.coe_injective
140	  change (sectionOfDivisor ⊤ D : Set X.functionField) = _
141	  rw [show sectionOfDivisor (X := X) ⊤ D = linearSystem D from rfl,
142	    linearSystem_eq_inf hcov D]
143	  rfl
144	
145	/-- **The unconditional Čech Euler characteristic.**  On a two-set cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`,
146	
147	`χ(D) = dim_k Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim_k Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim_k 𝒜(D)`.
148	
149	**No exactness hypotheses.**  The only inputs are the cover and the finiteness of the two
150	chart section spaces; `𝒜(D)`'s finiteness follows, since `𝒜(D) ⊇ B(D)` is not needed —
151	what is needed is that `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is finite-dimensional, which is the binder
152	`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)`.
153	
154	Proof: `ℓ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁)` (the cover, `sectionSub_top_eq_inf`) and
155	`h¹(D) = dim 𝒜(D) − dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁)` (rank–nullity for the quotient `𝒜(D)/B(D)`), so
156	`χ(D) = dim(S₀ ⊓ S₁) + dim(S₀ ⊔ S₁) − dim 𝒜(D)`, and the modular law
157	`Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` replaces the first two terms by
158	`dim S₀ + dim S₁`. -/
159	theorem chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
160	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
161	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
162	    chi k U₀ U₁ D = (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
163	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
164	      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) := by
165	  classical
166	  -- `h¹(D) + dim B(D) = dim 𝒜(D)`: rank–nullity for `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D) / B(D)`.
167	  have hcob : Module.finrank k (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)
168	      + Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
169	          (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
170	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
171	    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
172	  -- The comap of `B(D)` into `𝒜(D)` has the same dimension as `B(D)` itself,
173	  -- because `B(D) ≤ 𝒜(D)`.
174	  have hBeq : Module.finrank k (Submodule.comap (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype
175	      (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)) = Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D) :=
176	    (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (coboundarySub_le_overlap k U₀ U₁ D)).finrank_eq
177	  -- The modular law for the two chart subspaces.
178	  have hmod : Module.finrank k (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D)
179	      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField)
180	        = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D) :=
181	    Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq _ _
182	  -- `ℓ(D) = dim (S₀ ⊓ S₁)` by the cover.
183	  have hell : ell k D
184	      = Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D ⊓ sectionSub k U₁ D : Submodule k X.functionField) := by
185	    rw [ell, sectionSub_top_eq_inf k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
186	  rw [hBeq] at hcob
187	  simp only [chi, h1dim, hell]
188	  omega
189	
190	/-- **The unconditional χ-difference formula.**  The χ-jump between any two divisors is
191	the alternating sum of the two chart steps and the overlap step:
192	
193	`χ(D') − χ(D) = ΔS₀ + ΔS₁ − Δ𝒜`
194	
195	where each `Δ` is the difference of the corresponding dimensions.  Again no exactness
196	hypotheses.  This is the honest replacement for `ChiLedger.chi_add`. -/
197	theorem chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor)
198	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
199	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
200	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D')] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D')]
201	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D')] :
202	    chi k U₀ U₁ D' - chi k U₀ U₁ D =
203	      ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D))
204	      + ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D') : ℤ) - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D))
205	      - ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D') : ℤ)
206	          - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)) := by
207	  rw [chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D, chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D']
208	  ring
209	
210	/-- **A one-point bump does not change the sections over an open missing that point.**
211	`Γ(U, 𝒪(1·P + E)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(E))` when `P.point ∉ U`, because `Γ(U, −)` reads the divisor
212	only at primes meeting `U`.
213	
214	This is `LedgerClosure.sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap` with the overlap
215	`U₀ ⊓ U₁` generalised to an arbitrary open — the generalisation is what lets the same
216	computation be run at *all three* terms of the Čech count below. -/
217	theorem sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem (U : X.Opens)
218	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U) (E : X.WeilDivisor) :
219	    sectionSub k U (pointDivisor P + E) = sectionSub k U E := by
220	  apply le_antisymm
221	  · intro x hx
222	    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
223	    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
224	    refine Or.inr fun Q hQ => ?_
225	    have hQP : Q ≠ P := fun h => hP (h ▸ hQ)
226	    rw [← add_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne E hQP]
227	    exact ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx) Q hQ
228	  · exact sectionSub_mono k U (le_add_pointDivisor E P)
229	
230	/-- **The off-overlap χ-jump is exactly the ONE surviving chart step** — unconditionally.
231	
232	Let `P.point ∉ U₀`.  Then the bump `E ↦ 1·P + E` leaves both the `U₀` term and the
233	overlap term of `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` untouched (`P.point ∉ U₀` and
234	`P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`), so the entire χ-jump is carried by the `U₁` chart:
235	
236	`χ(1·P + E) − χ(E) = dim Γ(U₁, 𝒪(1·P+E)) − dim Γ(U₁, 𝒪(E))`.
237	
238	**Do NOT read this as rescuing `hbump`.**  An earlier version of this docstring did exactly
239	that: it noted that the surviving chart step is `≥ 0` rather than provably `0`, and concluded
240	that inbox `I-0449`'s refutation of `hbump` off the overlap had misfired — that the argument
241	measured `chi_add`'s hypotheses rather than `hbump`.  **That was wrong**, and §5 below proves
242	the opposite from this file's own formula: `hbump` is refuted off a chart *unconditionally*,
243	with no `chi_add` and no exactness hypothesis anywhere.  `I-0449` was right, and is now
244	strengthened from a conditional to an unconditional refutation.
245	
246	The error is worth naming because it is a general one.  A **one-step** identity constrains
247	nothing by itself.  The refutation lives in the **tower** `n·P`: iterating this same bump
248	freezes both `Γ(U₀,−)` (the point is off `U₀`) and `𝒜` (off the overlap), while
249	`Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜` is trapped — so χ is *bounded* along the tower, whereas `hbump` demands growth
250	`n·[κ(P):k]`.  See `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` and `not_bump_of_notMem_left`. -/
251	theorem chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
252	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
253	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
254	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
255	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
256	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
257	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :

123	`U ⊆ X` and a Weil divisor `D`, the set of rational functions `f ∈ K(X)` whose
124	order along every prime divisor `P` meeting `U` is at least `-D(P)`:
125	`Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f : f = 0 ∨ ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }`.
126

128	convention gives `ord_P 0 = 0`, so the zero function must be admitted separately).
129	Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric `order_add_ge_min`. -/
130	def sectionOfDivisor (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
131	    AddSubgroup X.functionField where
132	  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
133	    -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }

135	  add_mem' := by
136	    intro f g hf hg

139	    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hgne

145	    have hcg := (hg.resolve_left hgne) P hP

148	          le_min hcf hcg
149	      _ ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := order_add_ge_min P hfne hgne h0
150	  neg_mem' := by

152	    rcases hf with rfl | hf

194	    sectionOfDivisor (U₁ ⊔ U₂) D =

208	    rcases (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup).mp hP with hP1 | hP2

218	        ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)) :

220	  ext f

222	    mem_sectionOfDivisor]

10	
11	`WeilDivisor.lean` records that the sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`
12	proves the closed χ-ledger sorry-free (`RiemannRoch/ChiLedger.lean`: `chi_divisorSheaf`,

15	in Lean rather than in prose, because it is the one that looked fatal and is not.
16	
17	## The apparent obstruction
18	
19	The two projects' sheaf-cohomology carriers are annotated in **different universes**:
20	
21	* AJCR: `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule F n := Abelian.Ext (constModuleSheaf J R) F n`, declared
22	  `Type u`, over a **small** site (`Cohomology/ModuleKSheaf.lean:74`).
23	* AJC: `Scheme.HModule k F n := Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J _).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n`,
24	  declared `Type (u+1)`, over a general `[Category.{u,v} C]`
25	  (`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/Carriers.lean:51`).
26	
27	Both instantiate at the *same* site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat` with the *same*
28	coefficients `ModuleCat.{u} k`, and — inspecting the definitions — at the *same* constant sheaf.
29	A `Type u` and a `Type (u+1)` are not the same type, and a bare `LinearEquiv` between them is
30	not even statable, so the mismatch reads like a wall.
31	
32	## Why it is not a wall — three facts, each machine-checked
33	
34	1. **`HasExt.{u}` is synthesised at AJC's own site**, not merely assumable: see
35	   `Adelic/CechComparisonGate.hasExt_moduleKSheaf`.  So the *lower*-universe `Ext` exists in AJC
36	   already; nothing needs to be built for it.
37	2. **The `Type u` `Ext` typechecks in AJC at AJC's arguments.**  `extLowerUniverse` below is
38	   AJCR's carrier shape, written in AJC, elaborating.  So AJC's `Type (u+1)` annotation is a
39	   *choice* made by `Carriers.lean` (for a general site where the lower `HasExt` need not exist),
40	   not a constraint imposed by AJC's geometry.
41	3. **`finrank` is ULift-invariant** (`finrank_uLift`).  This is the fact that decides the port,
42	   because the χ-ledger's content is entirely *dimension* statements: `χ = h⁰ − h¹`,
43	   `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`, `deg (div g) = 0`.  A universe mismatch between carriers does not
44	   obstruct transporting an equation between their `finrank`s.
45	
46	## The audit verdict this supports
47	
48	The universe gap is an **annotation artifact**, not a mathematical obstruction: it costs a
49	`ULift` in the statement of a comparison, and nothing in the proofs.  It is therefore *not*
50	among the real costs of porting AJCR's ledger.  The real costs are the ones `WeilDivisor.lean`
51	names — the divisor index set (now closed, `CurveCoheight.equivNonGeneric`), the residue-degree
52	weighting of `deg` (discharged over `k̄`), and the genuine bulk: AJC has no `divisorSheaf`, no

54

56	which 7 files are outside its `RiemannRoch/`.  That is the cheap end of AJCR's 17.8k-line
57	`RiemannRoch/` by a factor of three (`UniformVanishing` needs 62 files / 16,750 lines;
58	`WindowFieldTransport` 139 / 39,929).  A multi-session port, but a port of sorry-free material
59	along identified comparisons — not a rederivation.
60	
61	## Provenance
62	
63	AJC-native; nothing is ported.  The three declarations below are AJC statements about AJC's own
64	carriers plus mathlib, written to make the audit's central claim checkable rather than asserted.

17	
18	**What this file does, and what it deliberately does not do.**  It does not re-prove
19	`coheight ≤ 1`: that rests on a ~180-line standard-smooth/Kähler-differential argument in
20	`Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean`, and duplicating it upstream would be worse than the problem.
21	Instead it takes the bound as an explicit **hypothesis** and packages everything else, so the
22	producer is available at *every* import level and the geometric input can be discharged wherever
23	it happens to be in scope:
24	
25	* `Scheme.PrimeDivisor.ofNonGeneric` — from `Order.coheight z ≤ 1` and `z ≠ genericPoint X`,
26	  build the `PrimeDivisor`.  Its `coheight = 1` field is `le_antisymm` of the hypothesis and the

29	  `X.PrimeDivisor ≃ {x // x ≠ genericPoint X}`, given the coheight bound at every point.  This

31	  mismatches `WeilDivisor.lean:1304-1311` lists as the cost of porting the sorry-free χ-ledger.
32	
33	The hypothesis form is the honest one here rather than a workaround: `coheight ≤ 1` is a genuine
34	curve hypothesis (it fails on any space of dimension `> 1`), so a producer that *assumes* it is
35	not weaker than one that proves it for a specific curve — it is the same content, reusable, and
36	it inverts no imports.  A consumer with `Adelic` in scope discharges it with
37	`Adelic.coheight_le_one_of_curve`; one without can carry it as a binder.

theorem isConstantField_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left where
  order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc := by
    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) :=
      C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk
        (⟨P.point, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
    haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
        C.left.functionField :=
      functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨P.point, trivial⟩
    have h1 : algebraMap k C.left.functionField c
        = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField ((constMap C).hom c) := rfl
    have hu : IsUnit (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
        ((constMap C).hom c)) :=
      ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hc).map (constMap C).hom).map _
    rw [h1, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)
      (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) C.left.functionField]
    exact Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit P hu

    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left :=
